publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice

articleTitle: Overhead line vertical galloping on bundle configurations: stability criterion and amplitude prediction
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The authors discuss a study which relies on a simulation program for the first three eigen modes of the vertical and torsional movements in a parametric approach to the phenomenon of galloping. Their aim is to discover the specific relations connecting the structural parameters of the lines liable to galloping. The determining factor is shown to be the torsion of the conductors. Three essential aspects are discussed: the use of four dimensionless parameters; a parametric study of the stability; and an original approach to the analytical predetermination of the maximum amplitudes. The critical range of the wind speed favourable to galloping is given. The calculations are made on the basis of the aerodynamic curves produced by various laboratories for ice coatings observed in the field. Finally the authors examine the effect of some anti-galloping devices (pendulums).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new type of compact line for urban and suburban areas
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The requirements for compaction of overhead lines in urban and suburban areas imply extra costs with respect to conventional lines. The new type of line proposed by the authors drastically reduces these extra costs. The new solution considers bidimensional towers with a pivoted base; conductors and ground wires contribute to the stability of the whole system. The frame type towers employ very slender and tubular-like elements which are built up on site by bolting together specially shaped cold formed steel sections. The very many calculations and tests carried out by the authors prove the high performance of the line. The first complete actual line of the new type (double circuit, 138 kV) was built in early 1987 and energized in Italy by ENEL. All the design, construction and operation criteria have been successfully confirmed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of a comprehensive plant and circuit database for design and maintenance planning
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: When faced with the planning, reconstruction, or maintenance of a power system complex inter-related data assembly tasks are undertaken. Inadequate or incomplete decisions, and engineering time spent on related data collection represent a regular and significant cost to all electricity boards. The authors identify the kinds of decisions necessary, and describe the evolution of a comprehensive database that can assist in the indentification of the total task, immediate access to all the relevant data, and direct data integration to relevant analysis, control and maintenance programs. The overall benefit of such a database will be to relieve the engineer of much time consuming clerical and routine data collection tasks. He will therefore be able to focus his efforts in areas where his experience and judgement as an engineer are of prime importance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new probabilistic approach to thermal rating overhead line conductors evaluation in the Netherlands
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: It is common practice among electric utilities to assess the nominal current ratings of overhead lines for power transmission and distribution by means of the deterministic method. This approach is only applicable to stationary situations, in which a set of fixed values for the worst combination of meteorological parameters and the design maximum conductor temperature have been assumed. However, by means of statistical modelling methods it is possible, on the basis of the expected load distribution, to determine the probabilities of exceeding the critical conductor temperatures. The research carried out so far is aimed at determining the conductor temperature distribution and estimating the possible consequences for the lifespan of the overhead conductor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical performance measurements of artificially and naturally aged polymeric insulators
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Polymeric insulators are widely used in North America as replacements for ceramic insulators in power overhead line applications. Such insulators are subjected to a variety of environments some of which can cause degradation of performance. The Canadian Electrical Association therefore sponsored a project to develop a satisfactory method of assessing the level of performance to be expected from a polymeric insulator over its lifetime in service. This project included the development of three different artificial aging procedures, using a set of insulators from four manufacturers as test samples. Insulators of the same design were energised at three sites with quite different characteristics to give naturally aged and polluted test specimens for laboratory measurements. Various diagnostic tests were used to measure the performance of the naturally and artificially aged insulators, and the results of these tests are discussed by the authors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High-voltage insulator designs using polymeric materials: performance under salt-pollution
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Types of polymeric insulators for overhead power lines and their associated terminal plant are increasing in number. The choice of design and material is now fairly extensive. The electrical performance in a moist, salt-laden atmosphere has been determined at the Brighton Insulator Testing Station for a wide range of products. The data presented, on insulators for system voltages below 150 kV (RMS), complement the information previously published for higher voltage levels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Transmission line developments up to 150 kV in eastern Australia
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Australian utilities have, over the past twenty years, experienced increasing difficulty in corridor acquisition for power transmission lines. The growth in load density has also required utilities to reinforce supply at higher transmission voltages. These pressures have forced utilities to consider the installation of transmission lines in road reserves, with circuits at voltages up to 150 kV being required in these corridors. The author summarises developments in line design for this voltage range in eastern Australia, and outlines methods developed for increasing capacity by line uprating. The reduction of visual impact is an essential element in urban line design, and the design responses to environmental pressures are also considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Refurbishing an up-rating a municipal 88 kV network
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Johannesburg, the largest city and main business centre of the Republic of South Africa, has a total population exceeding one million and a maximum one hour peak demand for electricity of 1248 MW (winter 1986). Its electricity network, supplying power to an area of 544 km/sup 2/ is managed by the City Council of Johannesburg and is independent of the national network. The authors present a description of a refurbishment project which will uprate the municipal power network to 88 kV. The uprating plan, constructional techniques and contractual aspects are all discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Medium voltage (12-24 kV) ABC overhead insulated lines
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: An innovative compact self-supporting medium voltage aerial cable system has been produced which has been designed to replace conventional overhead lines especially where added system reliability is required. In Sweden, this design has been standardised for nominal 12-24 kV distribution system voltages and is known as AXUS. This system significantly reduces the demand for space, as line clearings can be narrow and multiple circuits can be attached to single poles. The 3 individually insulated phase conductors are helically twisted around each other to form a compact and robust unit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A unified theory for the design of pole foundations
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: A new ultimate pressure distribution model around the embedded part of a pole, under the action of a lateral load, is proposed. By introducing a new term called the lateral coefficient of contact pressure and applying the principles of equilibrium, a formula for the depth of embedment in soils is derived. For small pole rotations (less than 1 degrees ) it is shown that the coefficient of contact pressure is a function of the lateral coefficient of subgrade reaction. Thus a unified formula is obtained for the depth of embedment in any soil. A 'normal pole foundation' is defined and a design chart is presented for the rapid design of these foundations. This formula gives excellent results when compared with the empirical and semiempirical data published in statutory regulations, overseas codes of practice, as well as the complex methods presented in textbooks on geotechnical engineering. Two worked examples illustrate the application of the formula.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Supports and foundations: variability and design
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: There are many factors which affect the behaviour both of wood poles and of the foundations which support them. Because both are basically of natural material there is also a considerable coefficient of variation which can be applied to each of the properties. In normal practice a simplistic view is taken of the shape and of the properties of the poles and foundations, yet a simple study shows the wide variations which can occur. Because of this variability, much more concern needs to be given to the partial factors which need to be applied to both poles and to foundations to ensure the correct coordination of strengths. The authors discuss these factors and how they affect design of wood poles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development and introduction of aerial bundled cables in Australia
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Aerial bundled cables (ABC) have been introduced into Australian power systems progressively since 1983. The development of ABC systems has been accompanied by an unprecedented drive to standardise ABC materials by both user utilities and manufacturers. The authors describe the introduction of ABC systems into Australia, with particular reference to work carried out by the Electricity Trust of South Australia (ETSA), the State Electricity Commission of Victoria (SECV) and The South East Queensland Electricity Board (SEQEB).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of a high performance vibration damper for alloy conductors
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: In the construction or refurbishment of high voltage transmission lines there is a trend away from traditional ACSR conductor construction towards conductors which use only aluminium alloy strands. However, due to the distribution of load in the newer AAAC construction conductors, the damping inherent in the conductors is substantially less than that of an equivalent ACSR conductor. The authors use an energy balance technique to examine the behaviour of a typical ACSR conductor and conventional Stockbridge damper arrangement which has been proven by many years of field service. The authors consider the suitability of the conventional dampers for use on the newer AAAC conductors, and also examine the behaviour of the AAAC conductor with an alternative, more modern damper design and conclude that potential problems exist if ACSR damping arrangements are used on the AAAC conductors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polymeric additions to HV conductors: some discharge effects
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: On traditional HV overhead lines, the fittings attached to the live conductors, such as spacers, have been largely metallic. The modern tendency, however, is to use polymeric additions, not only as spacers but also as aerodynamic spoilers, bird-flight diverters and bale hangers. It has long been realised that metallic fittings may cause stress concentrations and hence discharges, if they have sharply curved projections. Polymeric additions are known to reduce this phenomenon to some degree. The work described by the authors is aimed at measuring the scale of this effect and giving some guidance to designers on likely levels of stress for the inception of visual discharges.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A personal computer based design system for profiling overhead lines
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: An efficient personal computer-based tool is presented for the mechanical dimensioning of overhead distribution lines. The design system includes routines for calculating the strengths of poles and conductors, calculating the sag curves, dimensioning the poles, cross-arms and stays and for the scaled graphical output of ground and line profiles. The design method also includes a simple heuristic optimisation algorithm for minimising the heights of poles within the safety and technical constraints. The programs are interactive and are equipped with graphic facilities. The experience of using the design method in practical design work has been very positive. Savings have been made both in the costs of building the line and in the time required for the design process compared with manual methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aeolian vibrations: possible effects of nonlinear behaviour of Stockbridge dampers
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The measurement of aeolian vibrations which were carried out in situ convinced the authors that the efficiency of Stockbridge dampers was not solely connected with the amount of energy which they could absorb. In fact it is possible to have an aeolian vibration damping mechanism based on the distortion of reflected waves by dampers with no other stresses for the end of span impedances than the existence of high nonlinearities. One of the nonlinearities due to Stockbridge dampers which is important is the coupling which they provide between two modes of protected spans. Te function of this coupling is difficult to demonstrate theoretically. In practice, the authors were able to verify that counterweights which do not dissipate energy but which produced a coupling of the same type are also good disturbers of aeolian vibrations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance of suspension insulators under flashover conditions
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: High-voltage outdoor insulators for power overhead line applications are subject to pollution by dirt and chemicals in industrial areas, and by salt deposits near the coast. In such a case, nonuniform heating of the pollution layer occurs at narrow sections of the insulators where the current density in the pollution layer is highest. Since almost the whole of the insulator voltage appears across these 'dry bands', air breakdown occurs, with the result of a quasistable gas discharge burn on the surface of the insulator, the current being limited by the series resistance of the pollution films. The author investigates this pollution flashover phenomenon by presenting a flat plate model for a cap and pin insulator. The dimensions of the suggested model are calculated. Using this model, the potential and field distribution on the polluted suspension insulator are determined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparative stress-strain characteristics of ACSR and SDC overhead conductors
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The control of aeolian vibration has been a concern of overhead electrical transmission line designers for at least 50 years. Various techniques, including the use of vibration dampers, lower stringing tensions, and conductor reinforcement at support points, have been used to combat aeolian vibration and its effects. Unfortunately all of these approaches require the use of additional hardware and consequently add to the overall cost of the transmission line. Self-damping conductors (SDC), however, have been used in North America for approximately 20 years and have a proven history of providing effective and cost competitive control of aeolian vibration without the use of additional hardware. In addition to giving some background information on the causes, effects and conventional means of controlling aeolian vibration, the authors provide some details on the economic and technical advantages of SDC. Also, the results of experimental work comparing the stress-strain characteristics of ACSR and SDC are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The metallurgical significance of changes in production practices for overhead line conductor materials
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Aluminium based overhead conductors are the primary means of transmitting and distributing power in the UK. The author draws attention to changes in the processing of the aluminium wires that go into these conductors that have occurred over recent years, and explains the metallurgical consequences of these changes and the significance for the user. Two types of aluminium based conductors are used: ACSR, in which hard drawn electrical conductor grade aluminium wires are reinforced with a steel core; and all aluminium alloy conductors, AAAC, made up entirely of aluminium alloy wires. The developments related to the production of the hard drawn aluminium and alloy wires are considered separately. In the case of the hard drawn aluminium wires, research work intended to reverse the decline in quality resulting from the changes in the production route is summarised and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The dynamic loading of overhead conductors on 11kV lines
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The behaviour of overhead conductors under varying mechanical load conditions is of great practical importance in the operation of distribution systems. Consequently the field of sag/tension calculations under any combination of conditions is well developed, and has been widely practised by electricity supply industry for many years. However in recent years, some concern has been raised that aluminium based conductors do not always perform as expected. In addition concern about the effects of severe weather on distribution systems has been mounting. The author discusses the behaviour of conductors subject to severe weather conditions, and describes some experimental work currently being undertaken to investigate this area.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and construction of a 132 kV double circuit line over a route containing extensive uncharted mineworkings
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The authors examine the design and construction of a new double circuit 132 kV steel tower overhead line built by the North Western Electricity Board UK, over a 21 km route, to enable a power station to 120 MW capacity to be closed. By necessity the line was built over a route which had been subjected to extensive coal mining activity for a period of 400 years. The mineworking included both charted and uncharted deep shallow and opencast mining. Prior to the new line being built, an existing 132 kV lattice steel tower line in the same area was discovered to have been severely affected by mining subsidence, resulting in reduced ground clearances. The authors also describe the techniques used to refurbish this line, whilst minimising the cost and the period for which the line was out of service.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of new objective method for the final assessment of power pole serviceability
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: In a tight money market the ongoing exponential increase of word power pole condemnation rates and pole replacement costs requires the revision of present approaches to the management of power pole resources. The author presents the new purely objective pole inspection method incorporating an advanced computerised hydraulic equipment technology. This fundamentally nondestructive test technique pinpoints weak poles which are below the required strength and provides a definite proof check for safe poles thus improving dramatically the safety of the distribution network and reducing the pole replacement costs to an almost absolute minimum. It is envisaged that the application of the new method will provide at least a million dollar savings per annum for a medium size power utility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rational design criteria for weather induced loads (overhead lines)
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The complete break-through of the design methods on a probability basis has been prevented up to date by the lack of a suitable data basis and by the fact that the approximations employed in the calculations leave a large gap between the actual and the calculated risk of failure. Methods have been evolved for determining on a probability basis the weather-induced design loads of transmission lines, which permit the use of traditional meteorological observation data and their necessary supplementation. An extended programme of investigation has been conducted to perfect the methods of converting meteorological characteristics to transmission line loadings. The optimum return period of the design load-furnishing the lowest total costs-has been determined from an estimate of all costs expected during the lifetime of the transmission line. The relatively wide range of near-optimum solutions permits the introduction of other practical aspects.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aluminium alloy (6201, 6101A) conductors
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Although aluminium alloy conductors have been available for some 60 years, it is only in recent years that they have been used to any great extent in the UK for voltages of 132 kV and above. Aluminium alloys are those based on the aluminium-magnesium-silicon system, internationally designated as 6201 and 6101A. The metallurgy of the aluminium-magnesium-silicon system, as exploited by the conductor manufacturer, is described together with methods of manufacture, advantages and developments such as improved conductivity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developments in overhead line connector systems
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The authors briefly discuss the concern expressed over the physical workload experienced by overhead linesmen and how the design of connectors can help reduce the physical stress on the linesmen's bodies. The authors then put forward the case for cartridge lined wedge connectors. They comprise an outer 'C' shaped body into which the main and tap conductors are held in position by an inner wedge. The wedge is driven forward by a cartridge powered installation tool. The operation of such connectors is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 150 kV transmission lines on tapered steel poles supporting insulator crossarms in Greece
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The large increase in the use of electricity in Greece has resulted in an ever-growing electric power demand. The supply of substations, by high voltage overhead lines (OL), creates more and more problems, especially where they cross residential areas, as in suburbs of big cities. A type of support that is aesthetically pleasing and creates fewer problems to the environment makes the OL more acceptable. The Public Power Corporation (PPC) has decided to proceed with the design of a compact line, in order to reduce as much as possible the problems of right-of-way and also to decrease to a minimum the visual impact. The author describes the first compact line in Greece including the tapered steel poles, construction details, design philosophy, and insulator crossarms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low voltage bundled lines in ESB, Ireland
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Traditionally, the Electricity Supply Board (ESB) Ireland, used open wire low voltage lines. The phased introduction of low voltage bundled conductor lines commenced in 1981. They are now standard construction in the ESB. The authors detail the development and introduction of low voltage bundled networks and the significant economies which have accrued. The qualitative aspects, including safety, maintenance, aesthetics and live line working are also discussed. The authors place emphasis on the integration of the new system with the conventional approach and its performance over the initial seven year period.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Laminated wood structures in Norwegian transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: In Norway laminated wood has been in use as an alternative material for transmission line supports for about 20 years. Earlier it was used for crossarms only, later for the entire structure. It has mainly been used on 66 and 132 kV lines with medium size conductors. Laminated wood has several advantages, making it interesting as an alternative to traditional wood pole and steel lattice towers. Since the early 1980s the interest for using creosote impregnated laminated wood structures has been increasing in Norway. More than 700 structures have been built for different types of overhead lines and the experience so far has been very good. The author discusses laminated wood structures as an alternative to traditional wood poles and lattice towers with regard to mechanical properties and economy. Two 132 kV lines, one double circuit and one single circuit line, both with conductors 537.7 mm/sup 2/, are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aeolian vibration recording and control
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: A series of problems are encountered in the operation and maintenance of high-voltage overhead transmission lines (OTL), these being due to a large extent to the fact that such lines are permanently subjected to meteorological effects (lightning, ice, wind). In OTL some of these effects are of special importance, such as those derived from the generation of vibrations in the conductors under certain conditions as a result of wind action. Consequently, OTL projects should include a study of the probability of different types of vibrations occurring and the means to be installed in order to reduce them. However, it is desirable to have available methods that make it possible to contrast the factors considered in the project with the real inservice behaviour of the lines. The authors describe the work carried out by Hidroelectrica Espanola in this field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CAMELIA: a calculation program for mechanical dimensions of MV, LV overhead lines
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Electricite De France have recently developed the CAMELIA software package which takes into account the various mechanical properties of overhead lines used in power networks. This software incorporates currently used design methods and enables the behaviour of the lines to be checked. Because it is fast, simple to use and can be implemented on a microcomputer, this package provides the planner with the capability of conveniently choosing the most appropriate equipment from the vast range of products available and according to the hypotheses used. It is also a means of checking the correct dimensioning of an existing line. The main properties of this software are described by the authors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Representation of planned overhead lines-the optical impression on the landscape
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The construction of high-voltage overhead lines is becoming increasingly difficult, due to the growing awareness of the population to their environment. For this reason planners and authorisation agencies try to limit the visual impact on the landscape by selecting a suitable right-of-way. In the past with the absence of engineering methods to evaluate the visibility of the right-of-way, decisions had to be taken by subjective and qualitative criteria. The authors present the realistic representation of overhead lines in the landscape on a color-graphic-display supported by 3D-computer graphics package, 3DOG. The quantitative evaluation of the visibility of the planned right-of-way is also shown using a new algorithm of image processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Al 59-a Swedish standard for overhead aluminium alloy conductors with 59% conductivity (IACS)
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: For many years distribution and transmission lines have been designed using aluminum conductors steel reinforced (ACSR) or in some countries all aluminium alloy conductors (AAAC). Both types normally have a conductivity calculated on the total area of 53-54% copper (IACS). Since the mid-1970s the cost of producing electric energy has grown rapidly, leading to an increase in the cost of losses. An attempt to find new conductor material producing fewer losses in the network was started in Sweden at the beginning of the 1970s and led in 1979 to the release of a new conductor standard called Al 59, where 59 stands for its conductivity (IACS). The authors deal with the cost of overhead lines and criteria for the choice of conductors. A comparison is made between Al 59 and ACSR.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technology for replacing existing ground wires with multi-core OPGW
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The volume of information transmission is expected to increase with advances in protection for electric power systems, and effectively coping with this through the utilization of existing transmission facilities, involves the construction of transmission networks for a wide range of optical information by replacing overhead ground wires by optical fibre ground wires (OPGW) having an even greater number of cores. In order to realize such a system, various technological developments have been made for OPGW having multiple optical fiber cores to provide nearly the same performance as overhead ground wires, and also for replacement methods that do not damage the optical fibers. The authors present a report on the techniques used to replace existing overhead ground wires with OPGW.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control of conductors to prevent construction problems
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The increases in cross-section and number of layers have gone hand in hand with new problems, chiefly with stringing conductors, e.g. the loosening of layers, which may lead to making birdcage, inter-layer slip connections difficult and, in general, problems which may, in extreme cases, mean that the conductors cannot be laid. With the conductor tests normally carried out, as indicated in the standards, it is not possible to calculate the conductor's specifications as to its greater or lesser degree of loosening (stringing conductors problems). The study of the stringing conductors problems has been carried out using a new method based on traction-torsion tests so as to register the rotation moments in each layer according to the force applied. These tests also provide data on the distribution of forces between the conductor layers. The authors discuss the test procedure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The consulting engineer's function of field inspection and site management during construction of transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The author discusses the function of the consulting engineer as a site consultant in the construction of power transmission lines and substations. Various aspects of the site consultant's task are discussed and emphasis is placed upon the importance of the site consultant in acting as a go-between and mediator in the conflicting aims of the client and the contractor. Different types of construction contracts are mentioned with the site consultant's role in each. Several recommendations, which are based on practical hands-on experience are offered. The advantages of both the client and contractor for having a site consultant are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The construction of lines using helicopters
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Since the advent of the helicopter it has often been viewed by construction engineers as providing that, hitherto much sought after, skyhook. The passage of time has shown that to some extent their hopes have been realised but the lack of general use in civil engineering and in particular overhead line construction poses a number of questions namely, the roles in which they are appropriate and the reasons for their use. The author addresses the answers to these questions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of overhead electric lines for improved reliability
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Overhead electric lines are affected by wet snow and ice accretion in two principal respects. Conductors and support systems become more highly stressed and the aerodynamic properties of conductors, which affect the normal limits, are disturbed by wet snow or ice accretion and under such conditions the risk of conductor clashing is much greater. The author reports on work undertaken in the UK in the following areas: the development of methods of producing severity maps for the UK for levels of wet snow accretion and associated wind pressures which are likely to be experienced on low level lines erected on terrain of varying heights; a new method of modelling the clashing of conductors which are covered with wet snow and exposed to a gusty wind; a new basis for the specification of overhead line design loads; and the development of an inexpensive failure containment device and a simple failure containment policy aimed at reducing the risk of cascade line failure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The mapping of the risk of wet snow sticking on power lines over a period of 35 years
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: With the help of climatic records coming from the National Meteorological Center, 20 episodes of wet snow have been reconstructed which have affected the electrical distribution network in the Nimes region (France) over a 35-year period, and the accumulation of snow on the conductors in each of these cases has been modelled taking account of the spatial and temporal climatic variations. By superimposition of the results, a quantitative mapping of the risk of the event in terms of absolute frequency, of maximum overloads and of the number of cases with maximum overloads greater than 1, 3, 5 and 8 kg m/sup -1/, over 10, 20 and 35 years is obtained. This quantitative mapping of the zones at risk may be used for facilitating the application of a policy for the overhaul of electrical distribution networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and application of aerial bundled conductors for the UK low voltage distribution system
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The LV overhead system in the UK has more or less now reached saturation with only a minimal amount of new lines being constructed. However, this system which was largely constructed between 1930 and 1960 is now of an age where reconstruction is becoming necessary and this will be the major work for the next few decades. With greater reliance on electricity, rural customers are coming to expect a more reliable supply than has been given in the past and this can be given more easily and economically by the use of LV ABC (aerial bundled conductors) and the intrinsic safety of the system is an additional bonus. Although initially the higher material costs for ABC have been a factor in discouraging greater use of this system, these costs are reducing and given greater use should show even greater savings. Consequently it is the view of the authors that the use of LV ABC is the logical choice for replacing the existing LV overhead system, but to obtain its full economic advantage it is necessary to adopt this to the exclusion of any other LV overhead systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of the variation of the electric contact resistance of the conductor joints during operation on the reliability of the overhead lines
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: Apart from the impact or vibrating forces due to wind actions, the operating life period of the bolted joints used in overhead lines is affected by mechanical, thermal and chemical factors acting simultaneously on the joint which depend not only on the type of joint used but also on the temperature and pressure applied to the joint in a given atmospheric condition. The analytical procedure discussed by the authors gives a suitable simplified solution to this complicated problem based on experimental model tests which enable the designer to make a comparison between the operating life period of the joint under different operating conditions. The authors discuss the importance of using bolts with suitable locking nuts to withstand the forces applied to the joint due to wind actions. They also present the advantage of shielding the joint against solar radiation to reduce the surface of contact temperature rise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design and application of optical cables into overhead lines up to 150 kV
publicationTitle: 1989 International Conference on Overhead Line Design and Construction: Theory and Practice
abstract: The authors briefly review optical communication technology which has possible application areas within the electricity supply industry. There is a growing demand for optical cables to be incorporated in new lines and also a requirement for their addition on existing lines. The accumulated experience of the last decade has shown that, because of their interference free operation and the availability of all dielectric cables, optical fibre telecommunications systems are uniquely suited to power system use. Significant advances in design and installation techniques are described, and experimental and operational results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
